name: Forth Bridge
blurb: Completed in 1890 as the world's first major steel cantilever bridge · relentless repainting became so proverbial it entered the language as 'painting the Forth Bridge' — until a 2011 recoat finally came with a 25-year guarantee.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Forthrailbridgefromsouthqueensferry.jpg

name: Hawa Mahal
blurb: Built in 1799 for the women of Jaipur's royal household · its five-tier pink facade is pierced by 953 tiny windows yet is only one room deep behind them.
source: Wikimedia Commons: East facade Hawa Mahal Jaipur from ground level (July 2022) - img 01.jpg

name: Imperial Regalia of Japan
blurb: Mythologised since Japan's Kojiki chronicle was compiled in 712 AD · reportedly no reigning emperor has ever seen all three treasures together — they're kept apart, wrapped, and never publicly displayed.
source: Wikimedia Commons: 三種の神器 1200x1200.png

name: Van Gogh Museum
blurb: Opened in Amsterdam in 1973 to house the world's largest Van Gogh collection · its architect, Gerrit Rietveld, died nine years before its doors ever opened.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Van Gogh Museum.jpg

name: Independence Hall
blurb: Completed in 1753 as the Pennsylvania State House · both the Declaration of Independence and the US Constitution were signed under this one roof, eleven years apart.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Exterior of the Independence Hall, Aug 2019.jpg

name: Art Institute of Chicago
blurb: Opened for the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition · the two bronze lions added a year later are nicknamed 'Stand' and 'Roar' and get dressed in jerseys whenever a Chicago team makes the playoffs.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Art Institute of Chicago (51575570710).jpg

name: Lahore Fort
blurb: Rebuilt in red sandstone from 1566 under Akbar, with later Mughal additions including the mirrored Sheesh Mahal · one candle's flame there multiplies into a thousand reflected stars.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Lahore Fort view from Baradari.jpg

name: Tabula Rogeriana
blurb: Finished in 1154 for King Roger II of Sicily after 15 years' work · a giant silver planisphere of the same map, said to weigh over 100kg, was destroyed by rioters within years of its making.
attribution: TabulaRogeriana.jpg : Al-Idrisi (original map), Konrad Miller (current map) *derivative work: PHGCOM ( talk ) (rotation)
source: Wikimedia Commons: TabulaRogeriana upside-down.jpg
image_author: TabulaRogeriana.jpg : Al-Idrisi (original map), Konrad Miller (current map) *derivative work: PHGCOM ( talk ) (rotation)

name: Park Güell
blurb: Designed by Antoni Gaudí from 1900 as a luxury housing estate · only two of the planned 60 houses were ever built, and Gaudí himself lived in one for nearly 20 years.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Güell BCN edited.jpg

name: Egyptian Museum
blurb: Opened on Cairo's Tahrir Square in 1902 · Tutankhamun's treasures sat in the same un-air-conditioned display cases there for over a century before finally moving out in the 2020s.
source: Wikimedia Commons: 1897 bis 1902 wurde das Ägyptische Museum in Kairo gebaut. 04.jpg

name: The Motherland Calls
blurb: Unveiled in 1967 atop Mamayev Kurgan, the hill where the fiercest fighting of Stalingrad raged · at 85 metres tall it was, for over a decade, the tallest statue on Earth.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Волгоград. Мамев курган. Родина-мать зовет.jpg

name: The Little Mermaid (statue)
blurb: Unveiled in Copenhagen harbour in 1913 · she's been beheaded twice and lost an arm to vandals, yet remains one of the most photographed statues on Earth.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Petite sirène de Copenhague (conforme à la loi danoise).JPG

name: Très Riches Heures du Duc de Berry
variants: tres riches heures du duc de berry
book of hours of the duke of berry
blurb: Begun around 1412 by the Limbourg brothers for the Duke of Berry · all three brothers and their patron died within months of each other in 1416, leaving pages like this one unfinished for 70 years.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Anatomical Man.jpg

name: National Air and Space Museum
blurb: Opened on the National Mall in 1976, days before the US Bicentennial · it became, within its first year, one of the most-visited museums on Earth.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Smithsonian Air and Space Museum.jpg

name: Aachen Cathedral
blurb: Consecrated in 805 AD as Charlemagne's palace chapel · German kings were crowned inside for over five centuries, and in 1978 it became one of the first sites ever named a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Aachen Germany Imperial-Cathedral-01.jpg

name: Daigo Fukuryū Maru
blurb: Caught in radioactive fallout from the US 'Castle Bravo' H-bomb test in 1954 · the crew's ash-dusted return helped inspire that same year's Godzilla and ignited Japan's anti-nuclear movement.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Daigo Fukuryū Maru 01.JPG

name: Daria-i-Noor
blurb: Looted from the Mughal treasury during Nader Shah's 1739 sack of Delhi, likely a sister-stone to the Koh-i-Noor · at roughly 182 carats it's one of the largest pink diamonds on Earth.
source: Wikimedia Commons: The Daria-e Noor (Sea of Light) Diamond from the collection of the national jewels of Iran at Central Bank of Islamic Republic of Iran.jpg

name: The Kiss (Klimt)
blurb: Painted in 1907-08 during Klimt's 'Golden Phase' · real gold leaf went into the paint, a nod to his father's trade as a gold engraver, and the Austrian state bought it straight off the exhibition wall.
source: Wikimedia Commons: The Kiss - Gustav Klimt - Google Cultural Institute.jpg

name: Royal Palace of Caserta
blurb: Built from 1752 for the Bourbon kings of Naples to out-do Versailles · its 1,200 rooms later doubled as the royal palace of Naboo in the Star Wars prequels.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Aerial image of the Palace of Caserta (view from the south).jpg

name: Historic Fortified City of Carcassonne
blurb: Its double walls were massively rebuilt after a failed 1240 revolt against the French crown · the defeated rebels' descendants were expelled and had to found a new town across the river.
source: Wikimedia Commons: Cité de Carcassonne.jpg
